title: DeadDrop rate-limit buckets never reap idle identities
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: robustness

Spec 18.9: 6 POSTs per hour per OSCORE context. _prune_old_requests(context_id) only walks that one key, and only when check_rate_limit/record runs for it (deaddrop.py ~261-271). Empty lists are deleted; idle keys with old timestamps stay until that same identity posts again.

ConfessionsResource explicitly reaps stale rate buckets. DeadDropResource does not.

Evidence: N distinct bound identities each POST once. _request_times holds N keys forever (until process restart), even after every timestamp is older than 3600s, because no later check_rate_limit(context_id) is invoked for those ids.

Impact: rate-limit state grows with the number of OSCORE peers (and with test-injected ids) rather than with the 1-hour window. On a long-lived node this is unbounded RAM versus the 8KB/32KB drop budget.

Oracle: spec window is 1 hour; idle buckets must be reclaimable. See confessions.py _reap_stale_rate_buckets.
acceptance_criteria: Idle per-context timestamp lists older than the 1-hour window are dropped without waiting for that context to POST again. A sequence of distinct OSCORE identities each posting once must not grow _request_times without bound. ConfessionsResource._reap_stale_rate_buckets is a template.
